title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s White Day Part 3
text: White Day calls for a tenfold return?
“What kind of event is this that favors women?”

I couldn’t help but snap back. I mean, I’ve heard of a threefold return, but I’ve never heard of a tenfold return. Besides, even the threefold return is just an urban legend, right? I mean, if it were some cheesy guy like Motoyasu from back in the day, it wouldn’t be surprising if he actually did a threefold return. But at the very least, I hate women who demand a threefold return as if it were a given.
“Huh? Huh? But my mom and my childhood friend always told me, ‘You’re supposed to give ten times as much in return,’ so I just assumed…”

Oh, so it’s some kind of family rule? Ren’s actually pretty good-looking, and he seems to be quietly popular with the ladies. Maybe he was raised to believe, “You shouldn’t just accept something that troublesome so easily.” Or maybe they were just a bunch of Trash women looking to get a free ride. It’s scary that both possibilities are plausible.

Anyway, Ren’s childhood friend… I seem to recall he mentioned that she died protecting him when he came to this world. Since she doesn’t come up much in conversation, she probably isn’t a romantic interest for Ren. She’d probably show up in an extra route on a fan disc for an eroge or something. Whatever you do, don’t let her come to this world.
“Over the top.”

Yeah, I agree with the female knight. It’s way too much, both physically and emotionally. Getting this massive pile of candy and clothes just for a single piece of chocolate—that’s over the top in every sense.

It’s fine since he’s a hero who can easily make money in this other world, but in real life, if he had to pay back gifts like that, he’d go broke. And the recipient is clearly struggling with it too. Just as we’re talking about this, Ren turns around.
“Ah, Wyndia! Here—this is my Valentine’s Day return gift!”
Ren approaches Taniko, who’s just arrived, carrying an equally large bag. Taniko glances at the female knight, then pushes the huge bag away with her hand. Good thing she wasn’t the first victim.
“…I don’t need that much.”
“Ren, your world might be ten times as generous, but by my world’s standards, they say three times is the norm. Female Knight, what about you?”
“I’ve only ever received gifts on Valentine’s Day—I’ve never given one in return. But… I think I’ve heard something about three times the value.”
I don’t have enough information. No, wait—if giving three times the value were the norm in this world, I’d have to rethink things a bit myself. I turned my gaze toward Raphtalia and the others.
“Would you have preferred a three-times-the-value return gift?”
“Um… isn’t this already three times the value?”

Raphtalia was just in the middle of eating the Bûche de Noël I’d brought out for dessert. Well, if that’s fine by her, then that’s fine by me. It’s easier on me, too, and I think it suits Raphtalia just fine.
“There’s a huge difference in quality and taste between the homemade chocolates I made and these ones Naofumi-sama made… But is giving three times as much really the norm for a return gift?”
Hmm, so that’s how she saw it. Well, it’s kind of silly to say three times is an absolute rule, isn’t it? I guess it really comes down to the individuals involved.
“Oh my? Well then, maybe I’ll demand three times as much, too?”
“If you triple it, you’ll die from drinking, you know.”
That Sadeena—she’s still here? Even the whiskey bonbons we just had have a pretty high alcohol content. If she tripled it, she’d definitely die of acute alcohol poisoning.
“Seriously, is giving three times the amount the standard here?”
“It’s not unheard of, but it’s not a hard and fast rule.”
I figured as much. Wait a minute! If they’d run an ad beforehand saying, “Gifts for Filo must be three times the original amount!” wouldn’t their profits have doubled?

No, even I feel like I shouldn’t go that far. Otherwise, future generations would establish a rule in this world that White Day gifts absolutely have to be three times the original amount. I’m not Ren, but what if three times three became the norm? I can’t let that spread—for the sake of future generations of men. And ten times? That’s absolutely out of the question.
Taniko had only taken the candy from the bag Ren held out. The female knight did the same—she took only the bag containing the candy. You guys didn’t actually give them anything, did you?
“Uh… what about this?”
“It’s heavy.”
“I don’t want it.”
“Come on… I went to all this trouble to pick out things that would match Wyndia and Eclair.”

Ren hung his head, having been flatly rejected by both of them. True… it is way too much. If you’re given a massive amount of candy, clothes, and even accessories just for a single piece of chocolate, it’s only natural for the recipient to feel overwhelmed. Plus, since they didn’t actually give anything themselves, their guilt must be overwhelming. After all, they both turned me down while glaring at me.

Seriously, one of you should just take Ren in already. If he’s in a happy relationship, this annoying behavior of his will probably calm down a bit. As for me, now that I’ve started wishing for someone else to be in a happy relationship… I wonder what that says about me. Am I just a decent guy? Hmm… I feel like something’s off. I’m in a really mixed mood.
“Ugh… Ren, it’s not like I’m rejecting your feelings or anything. Right? Wyndia?”
“I don’t want him.”
“Wyndia!”
“I see… so that’s how it is. Haha, I’m sorry… Eclair, Wyndia.”
“Ugh… it’s not like I didn’t like him or anything.”
“I see! Well, then that’s fine!”

Ren is so optimistic. Still, these guys seem to be having a good time, despite everything. It’s kind of like a romantic comedy. You know, like those “unlucky in love” types that were all the rage a while back? It’s like that.
“Wouldn’t it be fine if we just paid them back threefold next year and called it a day?”
“…Even so, as a token of my daily gratitude, I’m preparing to pay them back tenfold.”
“I told you that’s too much!”
Ren really never learns… I feel like giving his so-called childhood friend a good lecture. Though I guess I’ll never see Ren again.

How did things turn out in Ren’s world again?　I seem to recall it being left vague. I wonder if Ren just suddenly went missing or something? It was supposed to be a world that had started to recognize the existence of other worlds… I can only pray that, as a result of scientific progress, they don’t end up invading us.
“Hm?”

As I was thinking about that, out of the corner of my eye, I spotted Itsuki giving Rishia some candy in return. And on top of that, he handed her a dress as well—Rishia was absolutely thrilled. …Are they close enough that he knows Itsuki’s dress size? These two were like this on Valentine’s Day, too, weren’t they? It’s all happening so casually, but aren’t they actually the ones enjoying it the most?

From Ren’s perspective, he must be incredibly jealous of Itsuki right now. Is this his way of thanking the girl who remained devoted to him even after he set a trap for her and kicked her out of the group? It sounds like the kind of heartwarming story you’d expect. Pfft!

I wonder why there’s such a huge disparity among the Heroes. I gave return gifts to almost everyone in the village. Ren tried to give ten times as much in return but failed. Itsuki is thrilled that Rishia accepted what was, in a sense, the “tenfold return” Ren wanted to give her. Motoyasu is… rushing out to buy up all the white chocolate to give to Filo as a return gift.

I’m starting to feel like I’m losing. Isn’t the amount I’m giving back way too much to begin with? Did Ren really intend to give this many gifts to everyone who gave him one? He received a fair number of obligatory chocolates, so he’d never be able to keep up. I can’t help but feel like Raphtalia is looking at Itsuki and Rishia with a hint of envy…
“What’s wrong, Naofumi-sama?”
“No… I’m not saying you have to give ten times as much, but did you want a gift that big?”
“Um…”
Raphtalia fidgeted, about to nod, but then looked toward me… or rather, behind me? and snapped back to her senses.
“N-no! This is plenty!”
Hmm… I wish she’d be a little more clingy, though… Well, I’ll try to be a bit more considerate from now on. I guess that’s what they call a man’s sense of responsibility.

By the way, Fohl and Atla, who still haven’t shown up, are out. They went off into the mountains with that old hag from the Hengen Muso Style. Apparently, Fohl is deeply remorseful about what happened last time and is disciplining himself so he never loses his mind again. As for Atla, I figured she was being forced to tag along—
Just as that thought crossed my mind, a chill ran down my spine.
“Na-Oh-Fumi-chan. Do you have any more of these candies?”
Just then, Sadeena stroked my butt. ――Flashback. The memory of nearly being stripped by the Chocolate Monster!
Chocolate clinging thickly to my legs. My legs sinking deeper. Chocolate tentacles crawling up my body. Chocolate shaped like dragon wings trying to envelop me, trying to strip me of my clothes…
Aaaaaah… Aaaaaahhhhh…!
“Lord Naofumi! Pull yourself together! Lord Naofumi, aaaaaah!”
It took me thirty minutes to snap back to my senses.

Once I’d regained my composure, I ordered the Chocolate Monster (now white chocolate), which had been wandering around in a daze, to be destroyed, and finally regained my composure. I feel like Gaelion is watching me from afar! Like I’m going to let her get away with that!
“Orca Girl! Don’t you dare do anything else that’s no joke either!”
“I think even my Big Sister is in pretty bad shape here… but I think Naofumi-chan needs this experience.”
“Just shut up! Hah…! Hah…!”
“Naofumi-sama, calm down! It’s almost time to leave.”
“Rafu.”
“Hmm… right.”
First things first: a quick recap. On White Day, there’s a joint musical event featuring Filo and Keel, as well as the Filolial Race. I plan to show up at both.

Well, as long as preparations are in order, the one with Filo and Keel should work out fine. The problem is the Filolial Race. Technically, we’ve already passed the preliminary screening the day before, so there shouldn’t be any issues.
“Guh…”
She’s asleep again. The Filolial I raised… why did she turn out so carefree? I’ve wondered this countless times, but I don’t think I’ll ever find the answer.
“Alright, you guys better do your jobs properly.”
As usual, Keel was hanging out in the village playing around right up until the last minute.
“I think you’re in charge of sound, right?”
“I’m supposed to create thunder effects.”
“Well, I’m off then.”
So she’s taking the orca girl with her… Well, I guess it’ll be fine.
“Alright, let’s go.”
I used my portal skill to teleport, and the rest of the group followed me to the venue in Zeltoble.
